adjudication_notes: Paper proposes a hybrid text+KG retrieval method to improve retrieval accuracy in a health-tech RAG application; only briefly mentions 'false retrieval' as motivation without principled analysis or mitigation of evidence reliability, distraction, conflict, adversarial, or calibration issues, so it is a general RAG improvement rather than a robust-RAG contribution.

C02_notes: Domain-specific e-commerce RAG method paper proposing a shared backbone with LoRA modules for retriever and generator. adjudication_notes: Domain-specific e-commerce RAG architecture (shared backbone with LoRA modules) and dataset paper; despite brief mention of noisy/conflicting user reviews, it does not analyze or mitigate evidence reliability, so coders' exclusion is correct while keeping the domain-specific failure type label.

title: Boosting the Potential of Large Language Models with an Intelligent Information Assistant
C02_notes: AssistRAG proposes an assistant LLM for memory and knowledge management to improve QA performance. While it includes a decision step on whether to use retrieved info, the focus is on boosting RAG capability rather than robustness, conflict, noise, or adversarial concerns. Background only.
C03_notes: AssistRAG is a general RAG enhancement framework with an intelligent assistant module for memory/knowledge management. While it includes plan-specification decisions ('Is Memory Useful?' / 'Is Knowledge Useful?') that touch on calibration/control, the primary contribution is improving complex reasoning QA performance via a trainable assistant plugin, not robustness under unreliable evidence. adjudication_notes: AssistRAG is a general RAG enhancement framework focused on boosting QA reasoning via an assistant plugin; its decision step on memory/knowledge usefulness only tangentially touches calibration and does not target evidence-reliability robustness, so coders' exclusion is justified.

title: C-3PO: Compact Plug-and-Play Proxy Optimization to Achieve Human-like Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: C-3PO proposes a proxy-centric multi-agent framework with agents that decide when to retrieve, filter retrieved information, and determine sufficiency for answering. Addresses adaptive retrieval control and noisy retrieval filtering, relevant to robust RAG.
C03_notes: ICML 2025 proxy-centric multi-agent framework for RAG. Three agents handle: (1) Reasoning Router decides retrieval necessity and complexity (adaptive/selective retrieval), (2) Information Filter selects relevant docs (noise filtering), (3) Decision Maker assesses sufficiency to answer or continue retrieving. Core contribution is calibrated control over when/what to retrieve and what evidence to trust. Tested on OOD datasets including FreshQA and MultiHop-RAG. Borderline robust-RAG paper—primary focus is alignment/performance, but the adaptive retrieval gating and information filtering meaningfully address calibration_control and noisy_retrieval. Includes as support.
adjudication_notes: C-3PO's multi-agent proxy controls when to retrieve, filters retrieved context, and decides answer sufficiency, which is fundamentally a control/calibration mechanism aligned with the calibration_control failure type.

title: Can Knowledge-Graph-based Retrieval Augmented Generation Really Retrieve What You Need?
C02_notes: Proposes GraphFlow for accurate/diverse KG-based RAG retrieval on complex queries. Focus is on retrieval quality/diversity for KGs, not on robust RAG axes like noise, distractors, conflict, adversarial corruption, or calibration. Mentions robustness only as generalization to unseen KGs. Out of scope.
C03_notes: Proposes GraphFlow, a GFlowNet-style framework for KG-based RAG that retrieves accurate and diverse knowledge for complex queries via flow estimator + retrieval policy. Contribution is a general retrieval method improvement for complex multi-step KG queries (accuracy + diversity), not an analysis/mitigation of unreliable evidence, noise, conflict, adversarial corruption, or calibration. Mentions robustness/generalization to unseen KGs only briefly. Closest taxonomy match is noisy_retrieval as it concerns retrieval imperfection, but it does not explicitly evaluate/mitigate noise. Out of scope.
adjudication_notes: Paper improves KG-RAG retrieval accuracy/diversity via GFlowNet-style policy; it does not analyze or mitigate evidence reliability issues (noise, conflict, adversarial, calibration), so it falls under domain RAG without a robustness mechanism and is out of scope.

title: Chunk-Distilled Language Modeling
C02_notes: CD-LM is a retrieval-augmented language modeling method focused on inference efficiency (multi-token chunk generation) and training-free domain adaptation via chunk distillation. C03_notes: CD-LM is a training-free chunk-level retrieval-augmented decoding method aimed at inference efficiency and knowledge adaptation (distillation/domain adaptation). General RAG/efficiency contribution; out of scope for robust RAG map.
adjudication_notes: CD-LM is a retrieval-augmented chunk decoding method for inference efficiency and knowledge adaptation; it does not study evidence reliability, noisy/adversarial retrieval, conflicts, calibration, or abstention, so coders' exclusion is correct.

title: Context Tuning for Retrieval Augmented Generation
C02_notes: Paper proposes context tuning to improve tool retrieval and plan generation in RAG. C03_notes: Paper proposes 'Context Tuning' to improve tool retrieval for underspecified/implicit queries in agentic RAG, using LambdaMART+RRF with usage signals. adjudication_notes: Both coders correctly identify this as a tool-retrieval enhancement method for agentic RAG with underspecified queries, lacking an evidence-reliability robustness mechanism, so it falls outside scope despite venue.

title: Cooperative Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Question Answering: Mutual Information Exchange and Ranking by Contrasting Layers
C02_notes: CoopRAG is a generic RAG framework improvement for multi-hop QA via query unrolling, contrasting-layer reranking, and reasoning chain completion. C03_notes: CoopRAG proposes a cooperative RAG framework combining question unrolling (with uncertainty masking), unrolling-augmented retrieval, contrastive layer reranking, and reasoning chain completion for single/multi-hop QA. Boundary case; primary lab noisy_retrieval as closest fit.
adjudication_notes: CoopRAG is a general cooperative RAG architecture for improving QA accuracy via query unrolling and contrastive-layer reranking, evaluated on standard QA benchmarks without a focused robustness mechanism for unreliable evidence, conflicts, attacks, or calibration, so coders' exclude decision is accepted.

title: Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs
C02_notes: Application paper on personalized agents using editable memory graphs with RL-based adaptive memory selection. Mentions noise from irrelevant memories and adaptive selection but does not systematically study RAG robustness, attacks, or evaluation. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

adjudication_notes: Both coders correctly identify this as a personalized agent application using EMG-RAG with RL-based adaptive memory selection; despite brief mention of noise from irrelevant memories, the core contribution is personalization and memory management, not robust RAG evidence reliability.

title: DSLR: Document Refinement with Sentence-Level Re-ranking and Reconstruction to Enhance Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: DSLR proposes unsupervised sentence-level re-ranking and reconstruction to filter irrelevant/redundant info from retrieved passages, directly addressing noisy retrieval and LLM distraction in RAG. Workshop paper at ACL KnowledgeNLP 2024, evaluated on open-domain QA benchmarks. Fits robust RAG context-refinement mitigation.
C03_notes: DSLR decomposes retrieved passages into sentences, re-ranks them, and reconstructs coherent passages to filter out irrelevant/redundant info that distracts LLMs. Explicit mitigation for retrieval noise and distractor content in RAG context. Workshop paper at KnowledgeNLP@ACL 2024.
adjudication_notes: DSLR is an unsupervised mitigation that decomposes, re-ranks, and reconstructs retrieved passages at the sentence level to filter noise/distractors before generation, which is a defense/mitigation operating at context assembly rather than at the retriever itself.

title: EAReranker: Efficient Embedding Adequacy Assessment for Retrieval Augmented Generation
C02_notes: Embedding-based reranker focused on efficiency/privacy and adequacy scoring; only tangentially touches filtering inadequate documents, lacks explicit robustness evaluation.
C03_notes: Efficient embedding-based reranker that scores document 'adequacy' (verifiability, coverage, completeness, structure) instead of pure relevance, claiming to filter inadequate docs that could mislead RAG. However, the paper's primary contributions are computational efficiency (constant memory, 2-3x faster) and privacy (no plaintext access), not analysis/mitigation of unreliable evidence, distractors, conflicts, or adversarial corruption. Borderline case; closest taxonomy fit is noisy_retrieval since it filters low-utility docs, but framing is general reranking improvement rather than a robustness-under-unreliable-evidence contribution.
adjudication_notes: Both coders agree the paper's primary contributions are computational efficiency and privacy (embedding-only access), with only tangential 'adequacy' filtering; lacks explicit robustness-under-unreliable-evidence evaluation, so exclude with context-assembly intervention if mapped.

C03_notes: Multimodal RAG retrieval improvement for OK-VQA via entity-focused dense passage retrieval. adjudication_notes: Paper proposes an entity-focused dense retriever for OK-VQA to improve retrieval quality; it does not address robustness to unreliable evidence, conflicts, adversarial attacks, or calibration, so coders' consensus to exclude is correct.

title: FiD-Light: Efficient and Effective Retrieval-Augmented Text Generation
C02_notes: FiD-Light focuses on efficiency-effectiveness tradeoffs in retrieval-augmented generation, not on robustness aspects such as noisy retrieval, adversarial attack, knowledge conflict, or calibration. While it briefly discusses robustness of source pointers to distribution shifts in #relevant passages, the main contribution is efficiency, not unreliable evidence, conflict, adversarial, or calibration. Background only.
adjudication_notes: FiD-Light is an efficiency-focused RAG method that compresses encoder-decoder information flow and adds source pointing; it does not study evidence reliability, conflict, adversarial attack, or calibration, so both coders correctly mark it out of scope and the intervention is on the generator side.

title: Graph-KV: Breaking Sequence via Injecting Structural Biases into Large Language Models
C02_notes: Graph-KV addresses positional bias and serialization issues in RAG by structuring KV-cache attention via source-target relationships. Evaluated on 7 RAG benchmarks including multi-hop reasoning and long-document understanding. Directly tackles context utilization robustness.
C03_notes: Graph-KV is primarily an architectural/efficiency contribution that modifies KV-cache attention to inject structural inductive biases for RAG and graph-structured data. It reduces positional bias and supports parallel encoding of retrieved chunks, with evaluation on RAG/multi-hop benchmarks. While it touches positional bias and notes noisy multi-hop reasoning, the central contribution is structural encoding/efficiency rather than analyzing or mitigating unreliable evidence (no retrieval noise, conflict, attack, abstention, or answerability analysis). Closest taxonomy fit is distraction (positional bias/context utilization), but out of map scope.
adjudication_notes: Graph-KV modifies LLM attention to reduce positional bias in RAG contexts; accept distraction per coders, generator intervention, retain in scope as appendix-level support.

title: Hierarchical Planning for Complex Tasks with Knowledge Graph-RAG and Symbolic Verification
C02_notes: Paper proposes a neuro-symbolic hierarchical planning method (HVR) that integrates KG-based RAG and symbolic verification for robotic task planning. RAG is used as a knowledge source for planning, but the paper does not study retrieval robustness, noisy/adversarial retrieval, knowledge conflict, calibration, or evaluate RAG robustness specifically. Robustness here refers to plan correctness via symbolic validation, not RAG robustness. Out of scope for robust RAG map.
C03_notes: Paper integrates KG-based RAG with hierarchical planning and a symbolic validator for robotic task planning. RAG is a knowledge source component, not the subject of robustness analysis. Symbolic verifier addresses plan correctness/failure detection (an agentic control mechanism) rather than unreliable retrieval evidence (noise, conflict, attack, ambiguity). Primary contribution is neuro-symbolic agentic planning; closest taxonomy fit is multimodal_agentic_code but the paper is not centered on RAG robustness under unreliable evidence.
adjudication_notes: Both coders correctly identify that KG-RAG is used only as a knowledge source within a neuro-symbolic hierarchical planner; the paper does not study retrieval robustness, noise, conflict, calibration, or adversarial evidence, so it falls outside the robust RAG scope.

title: Holistic Reasoning with Long-Context LMs: A Benchmark for Database Operations on Massive Textual Data
C02_notes: HoloBench benchmarks long-context LMs vs RAG on holistic reasoning over large textual data, varying context length, info density, position, and query complexity. Relevant to RAG evaluation and long-context distraction analysis, though framed as LCLM benchmark contrasted with RAG.

However, the main contribution is evaluating LCLM capabilities, not robustness of RAG under unreliable evidence. Boundary/background context only.
adjudication_notes: HoloBench varies context length, information density, and position to evaluate long-context reasoning explicitly contrasted with RAG, providing useful venue-supported boundary evidence on distraction/holistic reasoning relevant to robust RAG evaluation.

title: HyPA-RAG: A Hybrid Parameter Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for AI Legal and Policy Applications

adjudication_notes: Domain legal/policy RAG with adaptive parameter tuning and hybrid retrieval targeting RAG failure points; fits modality_scenario stratum with venue support.

title: Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation through Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
C02_notes: Paper proposes MMOA-RAG, a multi-agent RL framework to jointly optimize query rewriter, retriever, selector, and generator modules in a RAG pipeline. adjudication_notes: Both coders correctly identify MMOA-RAG as a general end-to-end multi-agent RL optimization of a standard RAG pipeline toward F1 reward, without any explicit robustness mechanism for noisy/conflicting/adversarial evidence or calibrated abstention, so it falls outside the robust-RAG scope.

title: KnowGPT: Knowledge Graph based Prompting for Large Language Models
C02_notes: KnowGPT is a KG-based prompting framework using RL and MAB for knowledge extraction and prompt construction. Out of scope.
adjudication_notes: KnowGPT is a KG-based prompting framework targeting search space, API cost, and prompt design rather than evidence-reliability robustness, so it falls under domain RAG without a robust RAG mechanism and is out of scope per the scope rule.

title: Knowledge-Consistent Dialogue Generation with Knowledge Graphs
C02_notes: SURGE proposes subgraph retrieval-augmented dialogue generation with KG, addressing irrelevant knowledge and hallucination via contrastive learning. While related to faithfulness and noisy retrieval, focus is on KG-grounded dialogue generation rather than robust RAG evaluation or attack/defense. Background relevance only.
C03_notes: KG-augmented dialogue generation (SURGE). Explicitly analyzes irrelevant retrieval (87% of 1-hop KG facts irrelevant) and proposes context-relevant subgraph retrieval plus graph-text contrastive learning to enforce faithfulness/consistency with retrieved knowledge. Addresses unreliable evidence (noisy KG facts) and hallucination, but in dialogue/KG setting rather than open-domain text RAG—hence support, not core.
adjudication_notes: SURGE addresses irrelevant KG retrieval and faithfulness in dialogue via subgraph retrieval plus contrastive learning, fitting domain/graph RAG with an evidence reliability mechanism.

title: Knowledge-Consistent Dialogue Generation with Language Models and Knowledge Graphs
C02_notes: SURGE is a KG-augmented dialogue generation method that retrieves relevant subgraphs and uses contrastive learning to enforce knowledge consistency. While it touches on filtering irrelevant facts and reducing hallucination, it predates the LLM-RAG robustness literature and does not explicitly study robust RAG attacks, defenses, or systematic robustness evaluation. C03_notes: SURGE: KG-augmented dialogue generation that explicitly tackles irrelevant retrieval (87% of 1-hop facts are irrelevant) via GNN-based subgraph retrieval and addresses hallucination/faithfulness via graph-text contrastive learning. Introduces KQA metric for faithfulness evaluation. Borderline support: not framed as adversarial robustness, but addresses noisy retrieval and knowledge consistency as core contributions.
adjudication_notes: SURGE explicitly addresses irrelevant KG facts via subgraph retrieval and contrastive consistency, fitting noisy_retrieval mitigation with mixed intervention; keep as borderline venue support.

title: LI-RAGE: Late Interaction Retrieval Augmented Generation with Explicit Signals for Open-Domain Table Question Answering
C02_notes: Paper proposes LI-RAGE for open-domain TableQA with late interaction retrieval and binary relevance token. Focus is on improving SOTA accuracy, not robustness to noise, attacks, or conflicts. Not a robust RAG contribution.

General RAG application; exclude from map.
adjudication_notes: Open-domain TableQA method (ColBERT late interaction + RAGE joint training + binary relevance token) targeting SOTA accuracy; the relevance-token filter is only tangentially related to evidence reliability and the paper lacks a systematic robustness contribution, so both coders correctly exclude it as domain RAG without an evidence-reliability mechanism.

title: LLM-Check: Investigating Detection of Hallucinations in Large Language Models
C02_notes: LLM-Check proposes hallucination detection using internal attention/hidden states/probabilities; explicitly includes RAG setting with RAGTruth dataset. Relevant to robust RAG via hallucination/faithfulness detection, though RAG is only one of several evaluation settings.

Not a core RAG robustness paper but a useful supporting tool.
adjudication_notes: Both coders agree the primary contribution is a hallucination-detection method enabling trust/abstention decisions (calibration_control), evaluated partly on RAGTruth; method_family stays as method/evaluation per canonical and C03, with generator-internal intervention.

C02_notes: M-RAG proposes a multi-partition RAG framework with multi-agent RL to improve generation quality on summarization, translation, and dialogue tasks. title: Modeling Uncertainty and Using Post-fusion as Fallback Improves Retrieval Augmented Generation with LLMs
C02_notes: Paper investigates uncertainty modeling (LLM 'unknown' outputs) and proposes post-fusion fallback and concatenation-as-distiller strategies to improve RAG when retrieved passages contain the answer but the model fails. C03_notes: Paper models LLM uncertainty via 'unknown' outputs and proposes post-fusion as fallback strategy when concatenation fails. Addresses calibration/fallback decisions (when to switch strategy) and distraction (LLM fails even when correct passage is in top-k under oracle setting). Multi-round feedback approaches. Workshop paper at KnowLLM 2024, useful support for robust RAG positioning.
adjudication_notes: All agree on calibration_control and inclusion; methods span context assembly via post-fusion, generator multi-round feedback, and system control fallback, so mixed best captures intervention point.
