Directly addresses ungrounded responses (knowledge conflict between LLM output and KB) and supports abstain/escalation control; introduces re-annotated datasets. Relevant as supporting evidence for robust RAG faithfulness detection.
C03_notes: Proposes RAGHalu, a two-tiered encoder-based hallucination detector for enterprise RAG that classifies LLM response sentences as VERIFIABLE/NO-INFO then SUPPORTED/UNSUPPORTED against retrieved KB articles. Addresses contextual faithfulness (response vs. evidence) and serves as a guardrail for human-in-the-loop escalation. Also releases re-annotated public dataset. Fits knowledge_conflict (contextual faithfulness) with secondary control and benchmark aspects. EMNLP Industry Track.
adjudication_notes: RAGHalu is a post-hoc faithfulness detector against KB grounding, fitting knowledge_conflict and defense/mitigation; detector operates on generator output for escalation.

title: Unified Generative and Discriminative Training for Multi-modal Large Language Models
C02_notes: Paper focuses on unifying generative and discriminative training paradigms for multimodal LLMs. While it mentions using RAG as a downstream strategy to enhance generative task performance, the primary contribution is on training methodology (Dynamic Time Warping, structure-induced constraints), not on robustness, evaluation, attacks, defenses, or calibration of RAG systems. No specific robust RAG angle.
C03_notes: Paper proposes a unified generative+discriminative training strategy (Sugar) for MLLMs to improve fine-grained semantic and retrieval performance. RAG is only mentioned as a downstream application enabled by the unified model. No contribution on unreliable evidence, retrieval noise, conflict, adversarial robustness, calibration, or evaluation of robust RAG. Out of scope.
adjudication_notes: Paper proposes a unified generative+discriminative training strategy (Sugar) for MLLMs; RAG is only a downstream application with no robust-RAG mechanism, so both coders correctly mark it out of scope.

title: WebBrain: Learning to Generate Factually Correct Articles for Queries by Grounding on Large Web Corpus
C02_notes: WebBrain introduces a dataset and ReGen framework for generating factual Wikipedia-style articles grounded on web evidence. While related to retrieval-augmented generation and factuality, it focuses on a new generation task rather than robustness analysis (no explicit study of noisy/adversarial retrieval, conflicts, calibration, or robustness perturbations). Background only.
C03_notes: Introduces WebBrain task/dataset and ReGen framework for generating factual Wikipedia-style articles grounded on web corpus. Focus is on hallucination reduction via better retrieval+citation+pretraining, not on specific unreliable-evidence robustness (noise analysis, conflict, attacks, calibration). Treated as background grounded-generation benchmark rather than core robust RAG contribution.
adjudication_notes: WebBrain introduces a grounded factual-article generation task/dataset and ReGen framework targeting hallucination via better retrieval/citation/pretraining, but does not study robustness to noisy/adversarial/conflicting evidence or calibration; coders' out-of-scope consensus is accepted.

title: Chain of Agents: Large Language Models Collaborating on Long-Context Tasks
C02_notes: Proposes Chain-of-Agents multi-agent framework for long-context tasks. RAG appears only as a comparison baseline; the paper is about long-context processing alternatives, not about robust RAG mechanisms, retrieval noise, or RAG evaluation. Touches lost-in-the-middle issue but not as a robust RAG contribution. Out of scope.
C03_notes: Proposes Chain-of-Agents multi-agent framework for long-context tasks (QA, summarization, code completion); uses RAG only as a baseline. Touches on 'lost in the middle' long-context focus issue but does not address unreliable evidence, retrieval noise, adversarial corruption, conflict, calibration, or robustness evaluation. General capability/efficiency method for long-context, not robust RAG.
adjudication_notes: Both coders independently judged this multi-agent long-context framework as out of scope; RAG appears only as a baseline and the paper does not address evidence reliability, retrieval noise, conflict, adversarial corruption, calibration, or robust RAG evaluation.

title: ChatQA 2: Bridging the Gap to Proprietary LLMs in Long Context and RAG Capabilities
C02_notes: ChatQA 2 builds a long-context plus RAG capable open model and evaluates on ChatRAGBench. Touches RAG robustness via chunk-size variation and top-k retrieval trade-offs (irrelevant context with large k), and explicitly compares long-context vs RAG. Primarily a capability/evaluation paper rather than a robustness-focused study, so support-level.
C03_notes: Primarily a capability-building paper for long-context LLM + RAG (extending Llama3 to 128K, training recipe, RAG vs long-context comparison). Mentions robustness to chunk size and analyzes top-k tradeoffs (fragmentation/irrelevance), but these are secondary findings, not focused on unreliable evidence, conflicts, adversarial inputs, calibration, or answerability. Closest taxonomy fit is noisy_retrieval, but contribution is general RAG/long-context performance.
adjudication_notes: Long-context RAG capability paper fits modality_scenario as case study with useful venue support; coders agree generator is the intervention point.

title: ChatQA: Surpassing GPT-4 on Conversational QA and RAG
C02_notes: ChatQA introduces ChatRAG Bench including unanswerable scenarios and conversational RAG evaluation; relevant to RAG benchmarking and answerability/abstention, though primary contribution is instruction tuning recipe for RAG/conversational QA.
C03_notes: ChatQA's primary contribution is a two-stage instruction tuning recipe to build a strong open conversational QA/RAG model competitive with GPT-4, plus ChatRAG Bench (10 datasets). It briefly addresses unanswerable questions/hallucination avoidance, but this is one of four contributions and not a focused robustness study under unreliable evidence. Treated as background general-RAG capability paper; unanswerable handling gives weak support relevance only.
adjudication_notes: Two-stage instruction tuning is a generator-side method paired with ChatRAG Bench including unanswerable scenarios, giving marginal robustness relevance via answerability.

title: Deliberation on Priors: Trustworthy Reasoning of Large Language Models on Knowledge Graphs
C02_notes: KG-RAG method using priors and introspection for faithful reasoning; not focused on robustness to noise, conflicts, or attacks.
C03_notes: KG-RAG method (DP) that improves KGQA accuracy via knowledge distillation of structural priors and a reasoning-introspection module that verifies extracted constraints and triggers backtracking. The 'trustworthy' framing is about faithful KG reasoning paths, not handling unreliable/noisy evidence, conflicting sources, adversarial corruption, or answerability. Closest taxonomy label is calibration_control due to introspection/verification with backtracking, but core contribution is a KGQA accuracy method rather than a robust-RAG-under-unreliable-evidence contribution; out of scope.
adjudication_notes: Both coders correctly identify this as a KG-RAG accuracy method using structural priors and introspection for faithful reasoning, not a robust-RAG-under-unreliable-evidence contribution; canonical's graph_kg scenario tag does not by itself confer scope without an evidence-reliability robustness mechanism.

title: Do Metadata and Appearance of the Retrieved Webpages Affect LLM's Reasoning in Retrieval-Augmented Generation?
C02_notes: Studies how non-textual metadata (publication time, source, visual appearance) of retrieved webpages affects LLM reasoning when documents present conflicting evidence in RAG. Directly addresses knowledge conflict and source preference in RAG; also introduces ConflictingQA-Fake dataset. BlackboxNLP workshop venue, useful supporting evidence for robust RAG map.
C03_notes: Studies how non-textual metadata (publication time, source credibility, webpage appearance) affects LLM reasoning when retrieved documents present conflicting evidence. Uses ConflictingQA and introduces ConflictingQA-FAKE. Core knowledge_conflict analysis with implications for adversarial manipulation (acknowledged in ethics). BlackboxNLP workshop at EMNLP 2024.
adjudication_notes: Paper analyzes how non-textual metadata (publication time, source, appearance) injected into context affects LLM reasoning under conflicting evidence; coders correctly identify analysis method and context-assembly intervention rather than canonical generator-level method/evaluation.

title: Optimizing LLM Based Retrieval Augmented Generation Pipelines in the Financial Domain
C02_notes: Empirical study benchmarks 6 LLMs across 15 retrieval conditions and 9 prompts on two financial RAG datasets. Probes robustness to missing gold docs, distractor count, and document ordering, plus prompt sensitivity. Relevant as evaluation/analysis evidence for retrieval-noise and distraction robustness in RAG.
C03_notes: NAACL Industry Track financial-domain RAG benchmark. Systematically varies retrieval quality (gold doc presence, number of retrieved docs, ordering) across 6 LLMs and 9 prompts to study impact on answer generation. Explicitly analyzes distractor documents and missing gold doc effects, plus pseudo-helpfulness/hallucination when evidence is missing. Fits noisy_retrieval (retrieval imperfection analysis) with distraction and evaluation_benchmark as secondary. Not a method contribution but useful empirical support.
adjudication_notes: Financial RAG benchmark systematically varies retrieval quality including missing gold docs, distractor count, and ordering, which best fits noisy retrieval evaluation rather than knowledge conflict.

title: Position: Retrieval-augmented systems can be dangerous medical communicators
C02_notes: ICML position paper analyzing pragmatic misalignment in medical RAG; decontextualization and selective context cause misleading outputs despite literal accuracy
C03_notes: ICML position paper arguing that RAG systems in medicine are 'pragmatically misaligned': even when individual facts are accurate, selective extraction and failure to reason about implicit query presuppositions/biases (e.g., 'why is X dangerous' vs. 'why is X safe', symptoms of disputed conditions) yield misleading outputs. Large-scale query study with LLM-as-judge evaluation. Primary failure framed as ambiguous/underspecified queries with implicit presuppositions (ood_uncertainty); also relates to selective context use (distraction) in a domain-specific (medical) RAG setting. Useful supporting/positioning work rather than a core method or benchmark resource.
adjudication_notes: Position paper on medical RAG pragmatic misalignment; ood_uncertainty captures implicit query presuppositions and ambiguity; analysis fits the position/empirical framing better than method or survey.

title: Reasoning-Enhanced Healthcare Predictions with Knowledge Graph Community Retrieval
C02_notes: Domain-specific KG-enhanced RAG for healthcare prediction (mortality/readmission on MIMIC). Focuses on improving prediction accuracy via KG community retrieval, not on robustness, noise analysis, adversarial attacks, conflicts, calibration, or RAG evaluation/benchmarking. Out of scope for robust RAG map.
C03_notes: KARE is a domain-specific healthcare RAG framework that uses KG community retrieval plus LLM reasoning for mortality/readmission prediction on MIMIC-III/IV. It motivates the work by noting traditional RAG retrieves 'sparse or irrelevant' info, but the core contribution is a new KG-construction + retrieval + fine-tuning pipeline for accuracy on clinical prediction, not an analysis/mitigation of unreliable evidence, conflict, attack, or calibration. Boundary multimodal/domain-specific RAG application; not core to robust-RAG map.
adjudication_notes: Domain-specific healthcare KG-RAG framework (KARE) for mortality/readmission prediction on MIMIC; the core contribution is KG construction plus community retrieval for accuracy, not analysis/mitigation of unreliable evidence, conflicts, attacks, or calibration, so it is out of scope for the robust RAG map.

title: Reducing hallucination in structured outputs via Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: Industry application paper using RAG to reduce hallucination in JSON workflow generation. Mentions OOD generalization and hallucination reduction, but it is primarily an applied system description, not a robustness study/benchmark/attack-defense. No analysis of retrieval noise, conflicts, distractors, or calibration mechanisms specific to robust RAG. Boundary/background only.
C03_notes: Industry application paper deploying RAG to reduce hallucination in structured JSON workflow generation. Trains a domain-specific retriever and fine-tunes LLM with retrieved context; main contributions are practical (reduced hallucination, smaller LLM footprint, OOD generalization) rather than a robustness/unreliable-evidence analysis. No study of adversarial inputs, knowledge conflicts, calibration, or noisy/distracting retrieval as an explicit research axis. Closest taxonomy fit is noisy_retrieval because of retriever-LLM alignment for entity grounding, but the paper does not analyze retrieval noise per se.
adjudication_notes: Both coders correctly identify this as an industry application paper deploying RAG for structured JSON workflow generation without an evidence-reliability robustness mechanism; falls under scope exclusion for domain-specific RAG applications.

title: SV-RAG: LoRA-Contextualizing Adaptation of  MLLMs for Long Document Understanding
C02_notes: SV-RAG is a multimodal RAG framework using LoRA-adapted MLLMs for long visually-rich document understanding. Focus is on efficiency and accuracy, not robustness, noise, conflict, or adversarial issues. Out of scope for robust RAG map.
C03_notes: SV-RAG is a multimodal RAG framework using LoRA-adapted MLLMs for long visually-rich document understanding. Focus is on efficient evidence page retrieval and QA, not on unreliable evidence, robustness, adversarial attacks, conflict, calibration, or answerability. VisR-Bench is a standard QA benchmark without robustness/perturbation axes. Out of scope for robust RAG map.
adjudication_notes: SV-RAG is a multimodal RAG framework for long visually-rich document understanding focused on efficient evidence page retrieval and QA accuracy, with no robustness, noise, conflict, adversarial, or calibration mechanism, so coders' exclusion is correct.

title: SearchLVLMs: A Plug-and-Play Framework for Augmenting Large Vision-Language Models by Searching Up-to-Date Internet Knowledge
C02_notes: Multimodal internet-augmented generation framework with hierarchical filtering and UDK-VQA benchmark; addresses up-to-date knowledge for LVLMs but not explicitly a robustness study.
C03_notes: Plug-and-play internet-augmented generation framework for LVLMs to access up-to-date knowledge via search engines. Includes hierarchical website/content filtering and a new UDK-VQA benchmark. The filtering touches on noisy web retrieval, but the paper's primary contribution is enabling multimodal IAG for fresh knowledge rather than analyzing/mitigating unreliable evidence, conflicts, or adversarial corruption. Boundary multimodal RAG application.
adjudication_notes: Multimodal IAG framework with hierarchical website/content filtering for up-to-date knowledge in LVLMs; primary contribution is enabling multimodal RAG rather than analyzing/mitigating evidence reliability, so out of scope per coder consensus.

title: Vgent: Graph-based Retrieval-Reasoning-Augmented Generation For Long Video Understanding
C02_notes: Vgent proposes a graph-based RAG framework for long video understanding. While it touches on retrieval noise and distraction from irrelevant clips, the focus is on improving video QA accuracy via graph structure and structured reasoning, not on systematic robustness analysis, attack/defense, or calibration in RAG. Best treated as adjacent multimodal RAG background, not core robust RAG evidence.
C03_notes: Graph-based RAG for long video understanding. Explicitly addresses retrieval noise and distraction by hard-negative retrieved clips via a structured post-retrieval reasoning/verification step. Robustness mechanism is tailored to the video/multimodal setting (graph over clips + structured query decomposition), so multimodal_agentic_code is primary with noisy_retrieval and distraction as secondary. Evaluation is mainly QA accuracy on MLVU/VideoMME/LongVideoBench, not a robustness benchmark per se, hence support rather than core.
adjudication_notes: Multimodal RAG with explicit robustness mechanism (graph structure plus structured post-retrieval verification to mitigate retrieval noise and hard-negative distractors), aligning with C03 and hidden case_study/useful_venue_support designation; intervention spans retriever and post-retrieval reasoning, hence mixed.

title: VimoRAG: Video-based Retrieval-augmented 3D Motion Generation for Motion Language Models
C02_notes: Domain-specific video-based RAG for 3D motion generation. While it addresses error propagation from noisy retrieval, it is not about robust RAG for LLM text/QA systems and falls outside the map scope.
C03_notes: Domain-specific (3D motion generation) cross-modal video-based RAG. Explicitly identifies and addresses error propagation from inaccurate/low-quality retrieved videos via McDPO, which teaches the LLM when to use/ignore noisy retrieved video signals. Robustness contribution is real but secondary to introducing the new motion-RAG paradigm; primary label set to multimodal_agentic_code with noisy_retrieval as secondary. Boundary support evidence for robust RAG under unreliable evidence.
adjudication_notes: Boundary case study: video-based RAG for 3D motion with retriever plus McDPO generator training to mitigate noisy retrieval; mixed intervention fits both components.

title: Visual Haystacks: A Vision-Centric Needle-In-A-Haystack Benchmark
C02_notes: Introduces Visual Haystacks benchmark for multi-image RAG, evaluates visual distractors and positional bias (lost-in-the-middle), and proposes MIRAGE visual-RAG framework. Relevant as multimodal robust RAG benchmark.
C03_notes: Vision-centric NIAH benchmark for multi-image QA; explicitly evaluates visual distractor susceptibility, multi-image reasoning failures, and positional ('lost-in-the-middle') bias in long-context LMMs. Also introduces MIRAGE visual-RAG framework as mitigation. Primary contribution is benchmark; distraction and multimodal RAG robustness are key axes.
adjudication_notes: Both coders correctly identify the primary contribution as a vision-centric NIAH benchmark (Visual Haystacks) evaluating distractor susceptibility and positional bias in multi-image QA, with MIRAGE as a secondary RAG mitigation; benchmark framing is more accurate than canonical multimodal_agentic_code.

title: A Theory for Token-Level Harmonization in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: ICLR 2025 paper provides theoretical framework for token-level trade-off between benefit and detriment in RAG, addressing noisy retrieval and knowledge conflict via Tok-RAG collaborative generation between pure LLM and RAG.
C03_notes: ICLR 2025 paper provides theoretical framework decomposing RAG token prediction into benefit (distribution completion) and detriment (distribution contradiction from noisy/incorrect retrieval). Proposes Tok-RAG, a token-level collaborative generation method that decides whether to trust RAG output or pure LLM at each token without training/evaluators. Primary contribution is a control/calibration mechanism for trusting evidence; addresses knowledge conflict between parametric and retrieved knowledge and noisy retrieval as underlying failure modes.
adjudication_notes: Tok-RAG is a token-level control mechanism deciding when to trust RAG vs pure LLM output, making calibration_control and defense/mitigation more accurate than canonical labels; underlying failures include knowledge conflict and noisy retrieval but the method's primary contribution is calibrated trust at generation time.

title: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation
C02_notes: FLARE proposes active retrieval that decides when (low-probability tokens trigger retrieval) and what to retrieve (anticipated next sentence as query) during long-form generation. This is a canonical adaptive/calibrated retrieval control method, directly relevant to robust RAG. Evaluated on multihop QA, commonsense reasoning, long-form QA, and open-domain summarization. EMNLP 2023 main conference.
C03_notes: FLARE proposes active/adaptive retrieval that triggers re-retrieval when LM emits low-confidence tokens during generation, and uses forward-looking next-sentence as query. This is a calibration-based control mechanism for when/what to retrieve (well-calibrated LM probabilities used as a trigger). Also notes that low-confidence tokens can distract retrievers (secondary: distraction). Evaluated on long-form QA and summarization.
adjudication_notes: FLARE is a canonical adaptive/calibrated retrieval control method using LM token confidence to decide when to retrieve and forward-looking next-sentence as query; canonical+C03 majority on method_family is retained though control/calibration would also fit.

title: An Information Bottleneck Perspective for Effective Noise Filtering on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: ACL 2024 long paper introducing an information bottleneck-based noise filter for RAG. Directly targets noisy/irrelevant retrieved passages, proposes SFT and RL training objectives, and evaluates on NQ, TriviaQA, HotpotQA. Core robust RAG contribution addressing noisy retrieval and context distraction via context-assembly filtering.
C03_notes: ACL 2024 long paper. Introduces Information Bottleneck principle to train a noise filter for RAG that compresses retrieved passages, explicitly removing irrelevant/noisy content while preserving info needed for the answer. Handles case where retrieval is irrelevant by compressing to empty. Directly targets unreliable-evidence (noisy retrieval) with defense/mitigation via context-assembly filtering. Evaluated on NQ/TriviaQA/HotpotQA for correctness and compression rate.
adjudication_notes: Paper proposes an information-bottleneck noise filter that compresses retrieved passages before generation, which is a defense/mitigation acting at the context-assembly stage, as both coders correctly identified against canonical.

title: Auto-GDA: Automatic Domain Adaptation for Efficient Grounding Verification in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: ICLR 2025 paper on Auto-GDA, domain adaptation framework for lightweight NLI-based grounding verification in RAG. Addresses faithfulness verification of LLM output against retrieved evidence, directly relevant to robust RAG hallucination detection and control.
C03_notes: ICLR 2025 paper proposing Auto-GDA, an unsupervised synthetic-data domain adaptation framework to train lightweight NLI models for grounding verification (faithfulness checking) of RAG outputs. Directly addresses hallucination/ungrounded generation by enabling efficient post-hoc verification that the answer is supported by retrieved evidence. Primary label is knowledge_conflict (contextual faithfulness); calibration_control is secondary because the verifier supports trust/abstain decisions.
adjudication_notes: Auto-GDA trains lightweight NLI verifiers to detect ungrounded RAG outputs, so the primary failure is grounding/faithfulness coded as knowledge_conflict, and the framework is a defense or mitigation operating as a post-generation system control check.

title: BEIR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of Information Retrieval Models
C02_notes: BEIR is a heterogeneous zero-shot IR benchmark explicitly targeting OOD generalization across 18 datasets and 9 tasks. Widely used as a retrieval robustness/OOD evaluation resource underpinning RAG retriever evaluation.
C03_notes: BEIR is a heterogeneous zero-shot IR benchmark covering 18 datasets across 9 tasks to evaluate OOD generalization of retrievers (lexical, sparse, dense, late-interaction, re-ranking). It is foundational infrastructure for retrieval evaluation but does not study RAG under unreliable evidence (no generator robustness, no conflict/adversarial/distractor analysis at the RAG level). Useful background for retrieval-quality framing but not a core robust-RAG contribution.
adjudication_notes: BEIR is a foundational zero-shot/OOD retrieval evaluation benchmark widely used as venue_backbone for robust retriever evaluation underpinning RAG; canonical+C02 inclusion is consistent with main_cite designation.

title: Benchmarking Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation with Dynamic VQA Dataset and Self-adaptive Planning Agent
C02_notes: Introduces Dyn-VQA benchmark for multimodal RAG with dynamic, multi-hop and time-varying questions, plus a self-adaptive planning agent (OmniSearch). Relevant as multimodal RAG benchmark and adaptive retrieval control.
C03_notes: ICLR 2025 paper proposes Dyn-VQA benchmark (rapidly-changing answers, multimodal, multi-hop questions) and OmniSearch self-adaptive planning agent for multimodal RAG. Addresses rigidity of heuristic mRAG: outdated vs. newer mixed knowledge and overloaded queries. Robustness contribution is in the multimodal agentic setting via adaptive retrieval planning; also serves as benchmark. Primary label set to multimodal_agentic_code since the mechanism is unique to multimodal agentic RAG.
adjudication_notes: Paper contributes both a multimodal RAG benchmark (Dyn-VQA) and a self-adaptive planning agent (OmniSearch); the robustness mechanism is unique to multimodal agentic RAG, with mixed intervention across retrieval planning and system control.

title: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine
C02_notes: MIRAGE benchmark systematically evaluates RAG components (corpora, retrievers, LLMs) for medical QA, including analysis of lost-in-the-middle effects and scaling. Provides domain-specific RAG evaluation resource relevant to robust RAG.
C03_notes: MIRAGE benchmark + MedRAG toolkit for systematic evaluation of medical RAG across 5 corpora, 4 retrievers, 6 LLMs on 5 medical QA datasets. Primary contribution is finding optimal RAG configurations for medicine. Touches on context-utilization (lost-in-the-middle effect, log-linear scaling) as secondary analysis, but lacks explicit focus on unreliable evidence, adversarial robustness, knowledge conflict, or selective answerability. Domain-specific benchmark; boundary context for robust-RAG map.
adjudication_notes: MIRAGE/MedRAG is a domain RAG benchmark, but it explicitly analyzes lost-in-the-middle distraction effects and log-linear context scaling across retrievers/corpora/LLMs, providing useful venue-level evaluation support for robust RAG; canonical and C02 inclusion is justified over C03's stricter boundary call.

title: Boosting Knowledge Utilization in Multimodal Large Language Models via Adaptive Logits Fusion and Attention Reallocation
C02_notes: ALFAR explicitly tackles knowledge conflicts between parametric and contextual knowledge in MRAG, plus attention bias (distraction-like) on retrieved context. Training-free generator-side intervention (logits fusion + attention reallocation) directly relevant to robust RAG. Multimodal setting is secondary.
C03_notes: ALFAR explicitly targets two robust-RAG issues in MRAG: (1) knowledge conflicts between parametric and retrieved contextual knowledge, and (2) attention bias diluting relevant context tokens. Training-free, plug-and-play generator-side method using adaptive logits fusion and attention reallocation. Shows robustness across varying contextual-knowledge quality (including noisy retrievals). Multimodal-specific but addresses core unreliable-evidence concerns.
adjudication_notes: ALFAR is a training-free generator-side mitigation (logits fusion + attention reallocation) that directly addresses parametric–contextual knowledge conflicts and attention bias in MRAG, so defense/mitigation fits better than the canonical method/evaluation.

title: Chain-of-Retrieval Augmented Generation
C02_notes: CoRAG trains LLMs to iteratively retrieve and reformulate queries to handle imperfect retrieval, with claimed robustness against retrievers of varying quality. Adaptive retrieval control relevant to robust RAG.
C03_notes: CoRAG trains LLMs to iteratively retrieve and reformulate queries, dynamically deciding next retrieval action based on state. Addresses imperfect single-step retrieval and reports robustness across retrievers of varying quality. Primary contribution is adaptive/iterative retrieval (calibration_control); secondary touches noisy retrieval mitigation. Not focused on adversarial or unanswerable settings, hence support-level.
adjudication_notes: CoRAG proposes iterative/adaptive retrieval with query reformulation and test-time decoding strategies, fitting calibration_control via system-level retrieval control; method/evaluation is more appropriate than defense/mitigation since the work is a general adaptive-retrieval method, not an adversarial defense.

title: ColPali: Efficient Document Retrieval with Vision Language Models
C02_notes: ColPali introduces a vision-language document retrieval model and ViDoRe benchmark. It motivates RAG pipelines but does not address robustness, noise, adversarial attacks, conflicts, or calibration. Background only for visual RAG retrieval.
C03_notes: ColPali introduces a vision-language document retrieval method and the ViDoRe benchmark for visually rich document retrieval. The contribution is about retrieval efficiency/quality on visual documents for downstream RAG, not about unreliable evidence, robustness, conflict, adversarial corruption, calibration, or answerability. Benchmark evaluates standard retrieval utility, no perturbation/threat axis. Closest taxonomy label is multimodal_agentic_code (multimodal RAG setting) but no robustness mechanism specific to the setting; out of scope for robust RAG map.
adjudication_notes: ColPali presents a visual document retrieval model and ViDoRe benchmark for retrieval utility on visually rich documents, with no robustness, noise, conflict, adversarial, or calibration mechanism, so coders' out-of-scope decision is correct.

title: DRAGIN: Dynamic Retrieval Augmented Generation based on the Real-time Information Needs of Large Language Models
C02_notes: DRAGIN proposes dynamic RAG deciding when and what to retrieve via real-time information needs detection and self-attention query formulation; addresses calibrated retrieval activation to avoid noisy unnecessary retrieval. ACL 2024 long paper, core evidence for adaptive retrieval control in robust RAG.
C03_notes: DRAGIN is a dynamic/adaptive RAG framework that decides WHEN to retrieve (via token entropy + self-attention importance via RIND) and WHAT to retrieve (via QFS over full context). Explicit motivation includes avoiding unnecessary retrieval that 'may introduce irrelevant or noisy data to LLMs which could jeopardize the quality of the outputs.' Fits calibration_control (adaptive retrieval / selective triggering). Secondary tie to noisy_retrieval as a motivation. ACL long paper; useful support for the calibration axis of robust RAG.
adjudication_notes: All coders agree on calibration_control/system control/in-scope; DRAGIN proposes a dynamic RAG method (RIND+QFS) for adaptive retrieval timing/query formulation, fitting method/evaluation over pure control/calibration as proposed by C03.

title: DeepDiver: Adaptive Web-Search Intensity Scaling via Reinforcement Learning
C02_notes: DeepDiver uses RL to adaptively scale search frequency/depth in iterative RAG over noisy real-web sources, explicitly targeting conflict resolution, verification/denoising, and reflection. WebPuzzle benchmark also evaluates robustness in real-web settings. Fits calibration_control with noisy_retrieval and conflict aspects.
C03_notes: NeurIPS 2025 paper introducing DeepDiver (RL framework for adaptive Search Intensity Scaling) and WebPuzzle benchmark. Explicitly targets real-web noisy/conflicting/unreliable sources and frames four behaviors: evidence gathering, conflict resolution, verification & denoising, reflection & correction. Primary contribution is adaptive when/how-much-to-retrieve decision-making (calibration_control); secondary contributions touch noisy retrieval, knowledge conflicts, and benchmark construction. Not a pure robustness paper but provides clear support evidence.
adjudication_notes: All coders agree on calibration_control/system control/in-scope; method_family kept as method/evaluation (canonical and C03) since the paper introduces both an RL framework (DeepDiver) and an evaluation benchmark (WebPuzzle) targeting adaptive search intensity over noisy real-web evidence.

title: Do You Know What You Are Talking About? Characterizing Query-Knowledge Relevance For Reliable Retrieval Augmented Generation
C02_notes: EMNLP 2024 paper presenting a statistical goodness-of-fit framework for detecting out-of-knowledge queries online and query distribution shift offline in RAG, directly addressing answerability and reliable retrieval.
C03_notes: EMNLP 2024 paper that proposes a statistical (goodness-of-fit) framework to detect out-of-knowledge queries (online) and query distribution shifts (offline) for reliable RAG. Directly addresses answerability/OOK detection and selective abstention, strong fit for ood_uncertainty with calibration_control secondary.
adjudication_notes: Paper's central contribution is detecting out-of-knowledge queries and query distribution shifts via GoF hypothesis testing, so ood_uncertainty with control/calibration method better fits than canonical calibration_control/method/evaluation.

title: Follow My Instruction and Spill the Beans: Scalable Data Extraction from Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
C02_notes: ICLR 2025 paper that introduces a prompt-injection-based data extraction attack on Retrieval-In-Context RAG systems, evaluates vulnerability across many instruction-tuned LMs and production GPTs, and proposes position-bias-elimination defenses. Directly relevant to adversarial robustness of RAG.
C03_notes: ICLR 2025 paper on prompt-injection data extraction attacks against RIC-based RAG systems. Demonstrates datastore leakage across many instruction-tuned LMs (Llama2, Mistral, Vicuna, etc.) and production GPTs; also explores position-bias mitigation as defense. Clear adversarial corruption threat model with attack+light defense; primary contribution is attack methodology and evaluation.
adjudication_notes: Both coders agree on adversarial_corruption and attack-primary framing for this prompt-injection data extraction work; position-bias elimination defense operates at context assembly stage, matching C03.

title: From RAG to Memory: Non-Parametric Continual Learning for Large Language Models
C02_notes: HippoRAG 2 is a RAG architecture paper using KG + Personalized PageRank for continual learning. While it mentions 'robustness' across factual/sense-making/associative memory tasks, it does not address robust RAG failure modes from the taxonomy (noise, distractors, conflicts, adversarial, OOD, calibration). It is a RAG method paper, not a robust RAG study.
C03_notes: HippoRAG 2 is a general RAG architecture improvement using KG + Personalized PageRank for non-parametric continual learning across factual, sense-making, and multi-hop QA. While it briefly notes that LLM-generated summarization noise hurts retrieval corpora, the paper's main contribution is a better retrieval/memory framework rather than handling unreliable evidence, adversarial corruption, knowledge conflict, calibration, or abstention. Out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence.
adjudication_notes: HippoRAG 2 is a KG+PPR RAG architecture for continual learning; it does not study evidence-reliability robustness mechanisms (noise, conflict, adversarial, calibration), so it falls outside the robust-RAG scope per the multimodal/domain-RAG exclusion rule.

title: G-Retriever: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Textual Graph Understanding and Question Answering
C02_notes: Introduces RAG approach for textual graph QA with GraphQA benchmark; mentions hallucination mitigation but primary focus is enabling graph QA, not robust RAG.
C03_notes: General RAG method for textual graphs (PCST-based subgraph retrieval) plus a GraphQA benchmark. Mentions hallucination mitigation but in the standard sense (retrieving relevant subgraph instead of hallucinating nodes/edges), not in the robust-RAG-under-unreliable-evidence sense. No analysis of noisy/conflicting/adversarial evidence, calibration, or answerability. Domain-specific (graph) RAG application, marginal to the map.
adjudication_notes: Graph RAG method with PCST subgraph retrieval; hallucination mention is generic, no robust-RAG mechanism for unreliable/noisy/conflicting evidence, so exclude per both coders.

title: GFM-RAG: Graph Foundation Model for Retrieval Augmented Generation
C02_notes: GFM-RAG proposes a graph foundation model for RAG retrieval. While it briefly mentions noise/incompleteness in graph structure, the primary contribution is methodological (GFM-based retriever for multi-hop QA), not a robustness study/evaluation/attack/defense. Out of scope for robust RAG map; closest taxonomy bucket is noisy_retrieval, but inclusion rule requires explicit analysis/mitigation of retrieval noise, which is not the central contribution.
C03_notes: Graph foundation model for RAG focused on multi-hop retrieval via GNN over KG-index. Briefly motivates by graph noise/incompleteness, but the contribution is a general retrieval method (scaling, generalization), not an unreliable-evidence robustness, calibration, or attack/defense study. Closest taxonomy bucket is noisy_retrieval but the paper lacks explicit robustness analysis under noisy or unreliable evidence. Out of scope.
adjudication_notes: Both coders correctly note that GFM-RAG is a general graph foundation model for multi-hop retrieval; it only briefly motivates with graph noise/incompleteness and lacks explicit robustness analysis, mitigation, calibration, or attack/defense, so it falls outside the robust RAG scope.

title: Generate-then-Ground in Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Multi-hop Question Answering
C02_notes: ACL 2024 paper proposing a generate-then-ground framework for multi-hop QA that explicitly mitigates retrieval noise and reconciles parametric vs. retrieved knowledge, fitting noisy_retrieval with a knowledge_conflict secondary angle.
C03_notes: ACL 2024 paper proposing GenGround framework for multi-hop QA. Explicitly motivated by noise in retrieved documents and the limitation of retriever performance. Generates answers from parametric knowledge first, then grounds in retrieved documents to revise. Addresses both noisy retrieval (primary) and parametric-vs-retrieved knowledge tension (secondary). Mitigation-oriented architectural change in the RAG pipeline.
adjudication_notes: GenGround framework explicitly mitigates retriever noise by generating from parametric knowledge then grounding in documents; noisy_retrieval primary with knowledge_conflict secondary, generator-side intervention.

title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
C02_notes: HippoRAG proposes a neurobiologically inspired RAG framework using knowledge graphs and Personalized PageRank for multi-hop QA. Focus is on knowledge integration and retrieval effectiveness, not on robustness aspects like noise, adversarial attacks, conflicts, or calibration. Not directly in scope for robust RAG map.
C03_notes: HippoRAG is a neurobiologically-inspired RAG framework using knowledge graphs and Personalized PageRank to enable single-step multi-hop retrieval. Focus is on knowledge integration efficiency and multi-hop QA performance (MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA), not on robustness to unreliable evidence, noise analysis, adversarial attacks, conflicts, calibration, or answerability. It is a general RAG architecture/efficiency contribution, out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence.
adjudication_notes: HippoRAG is a general RAG architecture for multi-hop QA via knowledge graphs and Personalized PageRank, focused on knowledge integration efficiency rather than robustness to noisy/unreliable evidence, conflicts, adversarial attacks, or calibration, so it falls outside the robust RAG scope.

title: Influence Guided Context Selection for Effective Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: NeurIPS 2025 paper proposing Contextual Influence (CI) value and a surrogate model (CSM) for selecting high-quality contexts in RAG, explicitly addressing noise robustness against irrelevant/noisy retrieval results. Has a dedicated 'Noise Robustness for RAG' related work section, discusses distraction, lost-in-the-middle, and over-trust of contexts. Filters context list adaptively (calibration aspect via positive CI value threshold). Evaluated on 8 NLP tasks with 2 LLMs.
C03_notes: NeurIPS 2025 paper proposing Contextual Influence (CI) value and a surrogate model (CSM) to filter poor-quality/irrelevant/redundant retrieved contexts. Directly targets noisy retrieval robustness; also touches distraction (negative marginal contexts) and parametric-vs-context redundancy/conflict (generator-aware metric). Clear defense/mitigation at context assembly stage.
adjudication_notes: Paper proposes Contextual Influence value and surrogate model to filter poor-quality retrieved contexts before generation, which is clearly a defense/mitigation operating at the context assembly stage rather than the retriever itself.

title: InstructRAG: Instructing Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Self-Synthesized Rationales
C02_notes: ICLR 2025 paper directly tackling noisy retrieval in RAG via self-synthesized denoising rationales used for ICL or SFT. Addresses imperfect retrievers/noisy corpora and shows robustness with increasing retrieved documents and OOD generalization. Clear core evidence for robust RAG map.
C03_notes: ICLR 2025 paper explicitly targets imperfect retrievers and noisy corpora. Proposes InstructRAG: LM learns explicit denoising via self-synthesized rationales (ICL or SFT). Tested on 5 knowledge-intensive benchmarks with robustness analysis against increased noise ratios and OOD generalization. Clear robust-RAG / noisy retrieval mitigation contribution.
adjudication_notes: Abstract explicitly frames the problem as imperfect retrievers/noisy corpora and proposes a generator-side denoising mitigation via self-synthesized rationales, supporting coders' noisy_retrieval + defense/mitigation labels over the canonical.

title: LongRAG: A Dual-Perspective Retrieval-Augmented Generation Paradigm for Long-Context Question Answering
C02_notes: LongRAG targets long-context QA where chunking disrupts global info and retrieval noise hinders factual detail identification. Proposes information extractor and CoT-guided filter to handle noisy/distracting retrieved chunks, directly relevant to robust RAG against noisy retrieval and lost-in-the-middle distraction.
C03_notes: LongRAG explicitly targets two RAG failure modes in long-context QA: (1) low-quality/noisy retrieval where substantial noise hinders identification of factual details, and (2) lost-in-the-middle distraction. It proposes a CoT-guided filter and information extractor as mitigations. Relevant to noisy_retrieval with distraction as secondary; EMNLP 2024 main paper.
adjudication_notes: Paper explicitly targets noisy retrieval and lost-in-the-middle distraction in long-context RAG via an information extractor and CoT-guided filter (mitigation); intervention spans context assembly and generator-side reasoning, so mixed is appropriate.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
C02_notes: Foundational TACL 2024 paper documenting the U-shaped position bias in long-context LLMs, with explicit multi-document QA and retriever-reader case study on NQ-Open. Directly relevant to RAG context utilization/distraction; introduces evaluation protocols showing performance degrades with middle-positioned relevant info and saturates well before retriever recall. Core evidence for distraction/long-context degradation in robust RAG.
C03_notes: Foundational TACL 2024 analysis showing U-shaped performance curve when relevant info is positioned in the middle of long contexts. Directly relevant to RAG distraction/context-utilization: shows that adding more retrieved documents (including distractors) degrades performance and that position of relevant evidence within context matters. Includes case study with retriever-reader on open-domain QA showing model performance saturates before retriever recall.
adjudication_notes: Paper analyzes position-dependent context utilization (U-shaped curve) and degradation from added documents, which is distraction/context-utility analysis via context-assembly manipulation, not knowledge conflict or a new generator method.

title: MMed-RAG: Versatile Multimodal RAG System for Medical Vision Language Models
C02_notes: ICLR 2025 paper on a versatile multimodal medical RAG system. Addresses robustness via domain-aware retrieval, adaptive context selection (filtering low-quality retrieved info), and preference fine-tuning to avoid interference from irrelevant retrieved content and reduce hallucinations. Fits multimodal_agentic_code as primary with secondary noisy_retrieval and calibration_control angles.
C03_notes: ICLR 2025 multimodal medical RAG system. Robustness contributions include (1) domain-aware retriever selection across radiology/pathology/ophthalmology, (2) adaptive k selection using similarity scores to filter low-quality retrieved contexts, and (3) preference fine-tuning to mitigate cross-modality misalignment and avoid interference from irrelevant retrieved info. Primary label is multimodal_agentic_code since mechanisms are tailored to multimodal medical setting; secondary covers calibration of retrieval, noisy retrieval filtering, and distraction by irrelevant contexts.
adjudication_notes: MMed-RAG proposes concrete mitigation mechanisms (domain-aware retrieval, adaptive context selection, preference fine-tuning) to reduce hallucination and misalignment in multimodal medical RAG, so defense/mitigation fits better than method/evaluation; other labels remain as agreed.

title: Measuring and Enhancing Trustworthiness of LLMs in RAG through Grounded Attributions and Learning to Refuse
C02_notes: ICLR 2025 paper introduces TRUST-SCORE metric and TRUST-ALIGN alignment for LLM groundedness in RAG, covering refusal calibration, citation faithfulness, and answerability. Directly relevant to robust RAG control/calibration and evaluation.
C03_notes: Introduces TRUST-SCORE metric and TRUST-ALIGN DPO-based alignment to improve LLM groundedness in RAG: correctly refusing when documents are insufficient, providing supported citations, and answering only from retrieved evidence. Directly addresses abstention/answerability and faithfulness under potentially insufficient evidence.
adjudication_notes: TRUST-ALIGN uses DPO to align the LLM (generator) to refuse appropriately and ground citations, making generator the correct intervention point over canonical system control.

title: MuRAG: Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generator for Open Question Answering over Images and Text
C02_notes: MuRAG is a foundational multimodal RAG method paper extending retrieval-augmented generation to images and text. While it evaluates under distractor settings, it does not analyze robustness, conflicts, attacks, or calibration. Background only for multimodal RAG positioning.
C03_notes: MuRAG proposes a multimodal retrieval-augmented transformer for open QA over images and text. The contribution is a new multimodal RAG architecture/training recipe, not robustness to unreliable evidence. Distractor setting is standard QA eval, not a robustness study. Out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence; treat as foundational multimodal RAG background.
adjudication_notes: MuRAG is a foundational multimodal RAG architecture paper; its distractor evaluation is standard QA, not a robustness/reliability mechanism, so it falls outside the robust-RAG scope per both coders.

title: PoisonedEye: Knowledge Poisoning Attack on Retrieval-Augmented Generation based Large Vision-Language Models
C02_notes: ICML 2025 paper introducing PoisonedEye, the first knowledge poisoning attack against Vision-Language RAG (VLRAG) systems. Injects a single poison image-text pair into the multimodal knowledge database to manipulate LVLM responses. Clearly an adversarial corruption attack on RAG with multimodal/agentic setting as secondary.
C03_notes: First knowledge poisoning attack on Vision-Language RAG systems; injects a single poison image-text pair into the multimodal knowledge database to manipulate VLRAG responses. Clear adversarial corruption contribution at ICML 2025; secondary label multimodal_agentic_code reflects the VLRAG setting.
adjudication_notes: Paper purely proposes a knowledge poisoning attack (PoisonedEye) on VLRAG with no defense, so coders' 'attack' label is more accurate than canonical 'attack/defense'.

title: Provence: efficient and robust context pruning for retrieval-augmented generation
C02_notes: ICLR 2025 paper on context pruning for RAG that explicitly targets robustness to irrelevant retrieved context, variable amounts of relevant info, and varying context lengths across domains. Directly mitigates noisy retrieval and distractor passages by dynamically pruning sentences before generation; also unifies pruning with reranking. Clear fit for robust RAG map.
C03_notes: Provence is a sentence-level extractive context pruner that dynamically removes irrelevant retrieved sentences (from zero to all) before LLM generation, explicitly motivated by mitigating propagation of irrelevant retrieved information. Tested for robustness across domains and varying context lengths. Fits noisy_retrieval (removing irrelevant passages) with distraction as secondary (reducing distractor influence on generation). ICLR 2025 venue backbone.
adjudication_notes: Provence is a defense/mitigation method (extractive context pruner) operating at context assembly stage to remove irrelevant retrieved sentences before generation, matching both coders' override of canonical labels.

title: RAG-DDR: Optimizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation Using Differentiable Data Rewards
C02_notes: ICLR 2025 paper proposes DDR, end-to-end DPO-based training of RAG modules to align data preferences, explicitly aimed at mitigating knowledge conflict between parametric memory and retrieved evidence and shown to generalize under added noisy documents. Robustness-relevant intervention on both knowledge refinement and generation modules.
C03_notes: ICLR'25 RAG optimization via DPO with rollout rewards over a two-agent (knowledge refinement + generation) RAG system. Explicitly motivated by knowledge conflict between parametric memory and external knowledge; also reports generalization to noisy documents during generation. Primary contribution is an end-to-end training/optimization method, but robustness to noisy/conflicting evidence is a stated outcome, so support-level inclusion with knowledge_conflict primary and noisy_retrieval secondary.
adjudication_notes: DDR end-to-end trains both knowledge refinement and generation modules via DPO to mitigate knowledge conflict and noisy documents, justifying defense/mitigation and mixed intervention over canonical.

title: RAGraph: A General Retrieval-Augmented Graph Learning Framework
C02_notes: RAGraph applies retrieval-augmented concepts to Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for generalization on unseen graph data (node classification, link prediction, graph classification). It is not about robust RAG for LLM systems, does not address retrieval/context robustness of LLM-based RAG, and contains no attack/defense, calibration, or RAG-specific evaluation benchmark. Out of scope for the robust RAG map.
C03_notes: General retrieval-augmented framework for GNNs to improve cross-task/cross-dataset generalization via toy-graph retrieval and prompt-based message passing. No analysis of unreliable evidence, adversarial corruption, conflicts, calibration, or robustness evaluation. Out of scope for robust RAG map.
adjudication_notes: RAGraph applies retrieval-augmentation to GNNs for cross-task graph generalization without addressing evidence reliability, conflicts, adversarial corruption, calibration, or robust RAG evaluation; both coders correctly flag it as out of scope.

title: RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: Proposes RE-RAG that adds a relevance estimator to provide confidence scores, enabling decoding strategies to abstain (unanswerable) or fall back to parametric knowledge when retrieved contexts are irrelevant. Directly addresses noisy/irrelevant retrieval, calibration, and answerability in RAG.
C03_notes: EMNLP 2024 paper proposing RE-RAG with a Relevance Estimator that produces confidence over retrieved contexts. Confidence is used for reranking, abstention ('unanswerable'), and falling back to parametric knowledge when context is irrelevant—core calibration/control contribution against noisy/distracting retrieval. Intervention spans context assembly (reranking) and system control (decoding strategy).
adjudication_notes: RE-RAG adds a relevance estimator that both reranks contexts (context assembly) and drives decoding decisions like abstaining or falling back to parametric knowledge (system control), constituting a defense/mitigation spanning mixed intervention points.

title: RECOMP: Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Context Compression and Selective Augmentation
C02_notes: RECOMP compresses retrieved docs into summaries and supports selective augmentation (empty summary when irrelevant), mitigating distraction and noisy retrieval in RAG. Directly relevant to robust RAG via context utilization and adaptive use of retrieval.
C03_notes: RECOMP compresses retrieved documents via extractive/abstractive summarizers and supports selective augmentation (empty summary when documents are irrelevant). Primary motivation is efficiency, but it explicitly mitigates distraction from irrelevant retrieved content and adds a control mechanism for when to use retrieval, so it provides useful support for robust RAG.
adjudication_notes: RECOMP is a mitigation method that compresses retrieved documents and supports selective augmentation at the context assembly stage to address noisy/irrelevant retrieval; coder consensus on method_family and intervention_point is well-supported, and noisy_retrieval (canonical+C03) is the primary failure addressed.

title: RankRAG: Unifying Context Ranking with Retrieval-Augmented Generation in LLMs
C02_notes: RankRAG instruction-tunes a single LLM for both context ranking and answer generation, motivated by the trade-off that larger top-k introduces irrelevant or noisy context. Directly addresses retrieval noise/distraction via reranking and filtering. NeurIPS 2024 venue makes it useful supporting evidence for robust RAG via context selection.
C03_notes: RankRAG unifies LLM-based reranking with answer generation. Explicitly analyzes top-k trade-off where larger k introduces irrelevant/noisy context that misleads generation (Fig.1), and proposes reranking to filter irrelevant contexts. Primarily a general RAG performance method, but mitigates noisy retrieval via context assembly. Borderline core/support; coded as support since unreliable-evidence handling is motivation but not the central robustness claim.
adjudication_notes: RankRAG proposes LLM-based reranking to filter irrelevant/noisy contexts before generation, which is a defense/mitigation operating at the context assembly stage between retrieval and generation.

title: ReDeEP: Detecting Hallucination in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Mechanistic Interpretability
C02_notes: ICLR 2025 paper proposing ReDeEP for detecting RAG hallucinations via mechanistic interpretability (decoupling parametric vs external knowledge contributions) and AARF for mitigation. Directly addresses faithfulness/knowledge-conflict robustness in RAG; core evidence.
C03_notes: ICLR 2025 paper. Proposes ReDeEP for detecting RAG hallucinations (where retrieved context is accurate but generation conflicts with it) via mechanistic interpretability, decoupling FFN-based parametric knowledge and attention-based external context utilization. Also introduces AARF mitigation method. Core knowledge_conflict between parametric and external knowledge in RAG; secondary calibration_control since it provides detection signal for trust/abstain decisions.
adjudication_notes: Paper proposes ReDeEP detection plus AARF mitigation method for RAG hallucinations arising from parametric vs external knowledge conflict, so defense/mitigation fits better than method/evaluation; other labels unchanged.

title: Reliable Decision‑Making via Calibration‑Oriented Retrieval‑Augmented Generation
C02_notes: CalibRAG explicitly tackles RAG calibration: forecasting function predicts decision correctness from retrieved documents, addressing overconfidence under noisy/irrelevant retrieval. NeurIPS 2025 venue, directly relevant to robust RAG calibration/control.
C03_notes: CalibRAG explicitly targets RAG overconfidence when retrieved documents are irrelevant/distracting. Proposes a forecasting function to predict decision correctness and rerank documents by decision confidence rather than relevance, producing calibrated confidence scores. Core calibration_control contribution; secondary touches on distraction (irrelevant docs misleading LLM) and noisy_retrieval (top-1 hit not optimal). Evaluated via ECE and accuracy on NaturalQA and other datasets. Intervention spans reranking (context assembly) and confidence output (system control).
adjudication_notes: CalibRAG is a calibration method (accept coders' control/calibration over canonical); intervention spans document reranking via forecasting function (retriever/context) and calibrated confidence outputs (system control), so mixed (C03) best fits.

title: Retrieval Augmented Generation or Long-Context LLMs? A Comprehensive Study and Hybrid Approach
C02_notes: EMNLP 2024 industry track paper that benchmarks RAG vs long-context LLMs across 9 datasets and proposes Self-Route, a self-reflection-based routing mechanism that decides when to use RAG vs LC. Relevant to robust RAG via adaptive control/selective retrieval and comparative benchmarking; analyzes RAG failure patterns and cost-performance trade-offs.
C03_notes: Comparative study of RAG vs long-context LLMs with a self-reflection-based routing hybrid (Self-Route) aimed primarily at cost efficiency, not robustness under unreliable evidence. The routing has some calibration/adaptive-retrieval flavor and the paper discusses RAG failure patterns, but the main contribution is performance/cost trade-off rather than handling noisy, adversarial, or conflicting evidence. Boundary context at best.
adjudication_notes: Paper proposes Self-Route, a self-reflection-based routing/calibration method that decides when to use RAG vs long-context, and analyzes RAG failure patterns—fits calibration_control with a method/evaluation system-control contribution, supporting canonical/C02 over C03's narrower scope read.

title: Retrieval Augmented Visual Question Answering with Outside Knowledge
C02_notes: Multimodal RAG method paper for OK-VQA proposing joint training of DPR retriever and answer generator. Discusses how irrelevant documents mislead training, but primary focus is on a foundational multimodal RAG architecture, not robustness analysis, attacks, conflicts, or calibration. No explicit robust-RAG angle.
C03_notes: Multimodal RAG application for OK-VQA proposing joint training of DPR retriever and answer generator. Briefly notes pseudo-relevance labels can encourage retrieval of misleading documents, but the main contribution is end-to-end training to improve VQA accuracy, not a robustness/unreliable-evidence study. Boundary multimodal RAG context, not core to robust-RAG map.
adjudication_notes: Foundational multimodal RAG architecture for OK-VQA focused on joint retriever-generator training for VQA accuracy; only passing mention of pseudo-relevance label issues, no robust-RAG mechanism, so coders' out-of-scope consensus is correct.

title: Retrieval is Not Enough: Enhancing RAG through Test-Time Critique and Optimization
C02_notes: AlignRAG addresses reasoning misalignment between LLM output and retrieved evidence via test-time critique; tests robustness under noisy retrieval. Core robust RAG contribution at NeurIPS 2025.
C03_notes: NeurIPS 2025 paper proposing AlignRAG, a test-time critique-driven alignment framework that trains a Critic LM to detect and correct 'reasoning misalignment' (divergence between LLM reasoning and retrieved evidence). Core contribution targets contextual faithfulness of generation to retrieved evidence and explicitly tests robustness under noisy retrieval scenarios. Generator-side mitigation via iterative critique with auto-stopping variant.
adjudication_notes: AlignRAG is a test-time critique-driven mitigation framework targeting reasoning misalignment between LLM output and retrieved evidence; coders correctly identify it as defense/mitigation at the generator, with knowledge_conflict as primary failure type.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
C02_notes: Foundational RAG paper by Lewis et al. (NeurIPS 2020) introducing RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token. It defines the RAG architecture and evaluates on knowledge-intensive NLP tasks but does not directly study robustness, noise, adversarial corruption, conflict, or calibration. Serves only as background/positioning for the robust RAG map, not as evidence for any specific robustness claim.
C03_notes: Foundational Lewis et al. 2020 RAG paper. Introduces the RAG framework (DPR + BART, end-to-end fine-tuning) and evaluates on open-domain QA, MS-MARCO, Jeopardy, FEVER. No explicit treatment of unreliable evidence, noisy/adversarial retrieval, knowledge conflict, calibration, or answerability. Serves as background/foundation for the map but is not itself a robust-RAG contribution.
adjudication_notes: Foundational Lewis et al. 2020 RAG paper introduces the RAG architecture but does not study evidence reliability, noise, conflict, adversarial corruption, or calibration; both coders correctly mark it as background/out-of-scope for the robust RAG map.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Perception: High-resolution Image Perception Meets Visual RAG
C02_notes: Visual RAG applied to high-resolution image perception in MLLMs with adaptive crop selection. Uses RAG mechanics but does not study robustness of RAG (no noise, distraction, conflict, attacks, or answerability analysis). Boundary multimodal RAG application, not robust RAG evidence.
C03_notes: Visual RAG applied to high-resolution image perception in MLLMs. Proposes Spatial-Awareness Layout for retrieved crops and RE-Search that adapts crop count based on model confidence/retrieval scores. Primary contribution is improving HR perception, not addressing unreliable evidence, adversarial attacks, knowledge conflicts, or robustness per se. The confidence-driven crop selection has minor calibration flavor but the paper is a multimodal RAG application; out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence.
adjudication_notes: Both coders correctly identify this as a visual RAG application for high-resolution image perception with no robustness mechanism against noisy, conflicting, or adversarial evidence; out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: Retrieving, Rethinking and Revising: The Chain-of-Verification Can Improve Retrieval Augmented Generation
C02_notes: CoV-RAG adds a verification module that scores references and answers, judges correctness, and triggers query revision and re-retrieval to mitigate external retrieval errors and internal hallucinations. Relevant as calibrated adaptive retrieval/control for robust RAG.
C03_notes: CoV-RAG introduces a verification module that scores reference and answer quality, judges correctness, and triggers query revision/re-retrieval when needed. Core mechanism is calibrated decision-making (verify→judge→re-retrieve) addressing both external retrieval errors and internal generation hallucinations. Secondary labels cover the retrieval noise correction and conflict between parametric/retrieved knowledge it targets. Findings EMNLP 2024.
adjudication_notes: CoV-RAG is a verification-based mitigation that scores references/answers, judges correctness, and triggers query revision/re-retrieval, spanning retriever, context, and generator stages, so defense/mitigation and mixed are more accurate than the canonical labels.

title: SEER: Self-Aligned Evidence Extraction for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: SEER proposes a self-aligned evidence extractor that filters distracting content from retrieved passages in RAG, improving faithfulness, helpfulness, and conciseness. Directly relevant to robust RAG via context filtering against distraction and noisy retrieval. EMNLP 2024 venue.
C03_notes: SEER proposes a self-aligned evidence extractor that filters distracting content from retrieved passages, framing the problem as separating supporting vs. distracting content. Uses faithfulness/helpfulness/conciseness experts. Directly addresses distraction and noisy retrieval as defense/mitigation at context-assembly stage. EMNLP 2024 main.
adjudication_notes: SEER is a model-based evidence extractor that filters distracting content from retrieved passages at the context-assembly stage, directly addressing distraction as a defense/mitigation method.

title: SePer: Measure Retrieval Utility Through The Lens Of Semantic Perplexity Reduction
C02_notes: ICLR 2025 paper introducing SePer, a semantic-perplexity metric to quantify retrieval utility via LLM belief distribution shift. Relevant to robust RAG evaluation as it provides fine-grained measurement of when retrieval helps or hurts.
C03_notes: Introduces SePer, a semantic-perplexity-reduction metric to quantify per-retrieval utility in RAG (knowledge gain to the LLM). Not directly about adversarial/unreliable evidence, but provides an evaluation tool that can flag low/zero-utility (irrelevant or distracting) retrievals, which is adjacent to noisy_retrieval and retrieval-quality assessment. Boundary support paper from ICLR 2025.
adjudication_notes: Paper introduces SePer, a semantic-perplexity-reduction metric to evaluate retrieval utility in RAG; coders correctly classify this as method/evaluation rather than benchmark/evaluation since the contribution is a metric/method, not a benchmark dataset.

title: Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: EMNLP 2024 empirical study of RAG workflow components (query classification, retrieval, reranking, repacking, summarization). Not focused on adversarial robustness, but provides systematic evaluation framework and identifies practices for filtering irrelevant context (reranking, summarization), which is relevant background for robust RAG pipeline design.
C03_notes: General RAG best-practices study that systematically compares modules (query classification, retrieval, reranking, repacking, summarization) for performance/efficiency tradeoffs. Does not focus on unreliable evidence, adversarial robustness, knowledge conflict, distraction, or calibration. Useful as background context on RAG workflow only.
adjudication_notes: Empirical study comparing RAG workflow modules end-to-end; better framed as benchmark/evaluation spanning mixed intervention points, retained as supporting venue evidence per hidden human decision.

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
C02_notes: Self-RAG trains an LM to adaptively decide when to retrieve via reflection tokens and to self-critique relevance (IsRel) and support (IsSup) of retrieved passages. Directly addresses calibrated/adaptive retrieval, faithfulness to evidence, and robustness to irrelevant context—core foundational work for robust RAG at ICLR 2024.
C03_notes: Self-RAG introduces reflection tokens enabling on-demand retrieval, relevance assessment (IsRel), support evaluation (IsSup), and utility scoring (IsUse). Core contribution is adaptive/selective retrieval with self-critique to handle unreliable or unnecessary evidence, directly addressing calibration and trust control in RAG. ICLR 2024 backbone paper for adaptive RAG.
adjudication_notes: Self-RAG is a defense/mitigation method that intervenes across retrieval (adaptive on-demand), context assessment (IsRel/IsSup critique), and generation (reflection tokens), so mixed intervention and defense/mitigation are better fits than the canonical labels.

title: Simple is Effective: The Roles of Graphs and Large Language Models in Knowledge-Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
C02_notes: SubgraphRAG is a KG-based RAG method focused on efficient subgraph retrieval and reasoning over WebQSP and CWQ. While it briefly mentions reducing hallucination and pruning irrelevant info, the core contribution is retrieval efficiency/accuracy, not robustness analysis under noise, distractors, conflicts, or adversarial conditions. Out of scope for robust RAG map.
C03_notes: SubgraphRAG is a KG-based RAG method focused on efficient and effective subgraph retrieval for KGQA (WebQSP, CWQ). It mentions reducing hallucinations and pruning irrelevant info ('lost in the middle'), but the core contribution is a lightweight MLP retriever with parallel triple scoring, not a robustness/unreliable-evidence/calibration/security mechanism. Out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence; closest taxonomy label is noisy_retrieval due to relevance filtering, with KG-RAG setting noted as secondary.
adjudication_notes: SubgraphRAG is a KG-RAG method focused on efficient/effective subgraph retrieval for KGQA; mentions of hallucination reduction and 'lost in the middle' are motivational, not a robustness-under-unreliable-evidence mechanism, so coders correctly mark it out of scope.

title: SmartRAG: Jointly Learn RAG-Related Tasks From the Environment Feedback
C02_notes: SmartRAG jointly trains a policy network via RL to decide when to retrieve, rewrite queries, and generate answers, directly addressing adaptive retrieval and calibrated decision-making in RAG.
C03_notes: SmartRAG jointly optimizes policy network and retriever via PPO. Policy decides when to retrieve, what to query, and when to answer directly — this is adaptive retrieval / decision-making, fitting calibration_control. Not focused on adversarial or noisy evidence robustness, but the 'when to retrieve' decision and reward design (minimize retrieval cost while answering correctly) places it as support-level in the unreliable-evidence map.
